row.evidence: Retool's pricing lists "SAML/OpenID Connect SSO, SCIM provisioning" only under Enterprise (custom pricing), and the docs return "SCIM is only available for Enterprise organizations" on other plans.
row.notes: Status unchanged (gated). Plan change since June: the June row put SAML SSO on Business, but the current pricing page shows Custom SSO (SAML/OIDC) on Enterprise only, alongside SCIM, and says Enterprise is required for SSO. Prices unchanged: Team $10/builder + $5/internal user per month annual ($12/$7 monthly); Business $50/builder + $15/internal user annual. Pricing is split by builder and internal-user seats; team_price_per_user_mo uses the builder seat. Retool API exists on Business with limited access, but the user and group endpoints are badged Enterprise in the API reference, so the user API is effectively Enterprise (api_tax). SCIM deactivation disables the user, logs them out and frees the billable seat. SCIM has no pagination and supports only userName eq filtering.

plans.name: Business
plans.notes: Retool API with 'Limited access' (user invites and user attributes endpoints are badged Business; users and groups endpoints are Enterprise). Audit logs UI included.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: Audit logs with streaming on Enterprise; no audit-log REST endpoint seen in the API reference.

auth.token_source: Settings > Retool API > Create new (token with SCIM API scope, permissions:scim); self-hosted may also set SCIM_AUTH_TOKEN env var (deprecated for child spaces)

operations.notes: No PUT on /Users in the spec; PATCH supports only 'replace' on name.givenName, name.familyName, active and user_type. Groups support GET, POST, PUT (replace members), PATCH and DELETE.

deprovision.data_retained: The account is disabled but left in place; on reactivation the user keeps all previously specified access controls.

custom.how: 'metadata' object on the SCIM user maps to Retool user attributes (Okta custom attributes with External namespace 'metadata'); capped at 1 MB. 'seatType' can set the seat type on plans with Named Seats; 'user_type' is PATCH-able.

roles.how: Group push; custom IdP groups can be mapped to Retool's default admin/editor/viewer/All Users groups

limitations.text: No pagination: count and startIndex are ignored.
Only userName eq filtering; users not provisioned via SCIM may have a null userName.
Entra ID needs the aadOptscim062020 flag on the Tenant URL to be SCIM 2.0 compliant.
Groups are matched by name, so a renamed IdP group appears as a new group in Retool.
User metadata payloads over 1 MB are rejected.

endpoints.purpose: Disable a user from the organization
Terminate all active sessions for a user
Create a user invite (Business and Enterprise)
Remove a user from a group
Assign a role to a user or group

rate_limits.text: Point system: up to 300 points per 60 seconds; Users endpoints cost 2 points, Groups and User Invite 5, Permissions 10; over the limit blocks API calls for 60 seconds.

limitations.text: Business plan has 'Limited access' to the platform API; users and groups endpoints are badged Enterprise in the API reference.

okta.notes: OIN page markup marks SAML, SCIM, Create, Update, Deactivate, Group Push and Group Linking as checked.

entra.notes: No Microsoft Learn gallery tutorial found (retool-tutorial and retool-provisioning-tutorial URLs return 404); Retool documents Entra SAML/OIDC SSO and SCIM via the generic endpoint with the aadOptscim062020 flag.

onelogin.notes: Retool has a OneLogin OIDC SSO tutorial; provisioning with OneLogin is not documented. OneLogin's own catalogue not checked (bot challenge).

fallbacks.other_sync: Google Groups sync via LDAP with Sign in with Google; SAML group sync and OIDC role mapping at login

Whether 'Orchestrated governance' event triggers (org invitations, password resets) count as user-event webhooks was not verified.
